extracted.intended_audience: Patent applicants and patent agents (Canada), including PCT national-phase applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance from the Canadian Patent Office (CIPO) on compliance with the Patent Act/Patent Rules and PCT national-phase entry requirements, including transitional rules, abandonment/reinstatement, representation, fees, translations, and examination timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing formatting (pre-June 2, 2007 option)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 3 applications with a filing date prior to June 2, 2007, may comply with the requirements for sequence listings found in the Patent Rules as they read immediately prior to June 2, 2007.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to the Patent Rules made on June 2, 2007 brought the formatting requirements for sequence listings in the Patent Rules in line with the PCT standard. Applicants for Category 3 filed before that date may choose the former formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement or declaration of entitlement (pre-Oct 30, 2019 option)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before October 30, 2019, an applicant may, instead of complying with the requirements in section 54 of the Patent Rules (SOR/2019-251), comply with the requirements surrounding submission of inventor and entitlement information that are in the former Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants choosing the former Patent Rules must consult the relevant ‘point-in-time’ version. PCT national-phase applicants may file a declaration as to entitlement under Rule 4.17 of the Regulations under the PCT (sections 225–227 of the Patent Rules (SOR/2019-251)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment after Oct 30, 2019 for failure to respond to prior requisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after October 30, 2019, an applicant fails to respond in good faith to a requisition sent before October 30, 2019 under sections 23, 25, 37 or 94 of the former Patent Rules, section 73 of the former Patent Act, as it read before October 30, 2019, will apply to the abandonment resulting from the failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional provision: abandonment/reinstatement consequences for requisitions sent under the former rules are governed by the former Act/Rules where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default common representative for joint applicants/patentees (transitional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are joint applicants and no patent agent is appointed immediately prior to October 30, 2019, a common representative will be appointed by default under the transitional provisions: the authorized correspondent under the former Patent Rules is deemed the common representative, or where an agent was revoked the first alphabetical joint applicant is deemed the common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent agent was appointed as of Oct 30, 2019 and later revoked, the first alphabetical joint applicant is deemed common representative. For patents, the former authorized correspondent at grant is deemed common representative. Joint applicants/patentees may appoint a common representative by a notice signed by all others; signatures of all required to appoint or revoke an agent unless agent signs revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of pre-Oct 30, 2019 appointments of patent agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appointment of a patent agent or associate patent agent made prior to October 30, 2019 in accordance with the former Patent Rules remains in effect after October 30, 2019 and is considered to have been made in accordance with the Patent Rules (sections 216 and 217).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 5 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures relating to granted patents started before Oct 30, 2019
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions in the Patent Rules (SOR/2019-251) regarding representation for procedures relating to a granted patent (section 37) will not apply to any procedure that started prior to October 30, 2019; the former Patent Rules continue to apply to such procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional protection: ongoing procedures follow the rules in effect when they started.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes due to College of Patent Agents and Trademark Agents Act (residency and firm appointments)
rubrics_metrics.description: As of June 28, 2021, patent agents must reside in Canada; appointments of non-resident agents are revoked. Firms are not considered patent agents; if a firm was previously appointed, all patent agents at the firm are deemed appointed in respect of the business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-resident agent had appointed a resident associate, that resident is deemed appointed as the patent agent. If a firm was previously appointed as an associate, its patent agents are deemed appointed accordingly depending on the appointing agent's residency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for priority made before Oct 30, 2019 remain valid
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for priority made in accordance with the former Patent Rules before October 30, 2019 remain valid after that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for priority for a Category 3 application may be made or corrected after Oct 30, 2019 within the time outlined in subsection 195. The request can be made in the petition or any separate document; Office strongly discourages making it in the abstract, specification or drawings. Requirement to provide copy/access to the priority application does not apply to requests made before Oct 30, 2019, but examiners may request a copy/access if they take it into account, with four months to provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of the right of priority — Category 3 restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration of the right of priority is not available for Category 3 applications (section 78.5 of the Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration of the right of priority is available for patent applications that have filing dates after October 30, 2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fee transitional application
rubrics_metrics.description: If no payment was made for a maintenance fee due before October 30, 2019, the former Patent Rules (section 73 of the former Patent Rules) will apply with respect to deemed abandonment and reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Otherwise, maintenance fees due after Oct 30, 2019 follow the amended section 27.1 of the Patent Act and the Patent Rules (SOR/2019-251).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 3 abandonment triggers (deemed abandoned conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Category 3 application is deemed to be abandoned if: (1) a notice under section 31 to appoint an agent is not complied with within 3 months; (2) applicant does not reply in good faith to request for further drawings under subsection 27(5.2) within 3 months; (3) applicant does not reply in good faith to notice under section 65 to modify due to non-compliance within 3 months; (4) applicant does not request continued examination and pay fee within 4 months of notice per subsection 85.1(3); (5) applicant does not pay the final fee within applicable times per subsections 86 or 199; (6) applicant does not reply in good faith to conditional notice of allowance and pay final fee within applicable time; (7) applicant does not comply with notice under subsection 155.5(6) requiring translation of certain parts of a PCT national phase application within 3 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These describe specific statutory/regulatory time limits that, if missed, cause deemed abandonment for Category 3 applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement after pre-Oct 30, 2019 failures not subject to due care standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant requesting reinstatement following failure to pay a maintenance fee or failure to request examination that occurred prior to October 30, 2019 is not subject to the due care standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 73 of the Patent Act as it read immediately before Oct 30, 2019 applies with respect to reinstatement in these circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination continuation (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of patent applications in progress will continue after October 30, 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing examinations are not interrupted by the coming-into-force of new rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting examination time limits (Category 3, s.197)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 197 specifies prescribed times to make a request for examination for Category 3 applications: regular national (not divisional) — five years after filing date; divisional with presentation date before Oct 30, 2019 — later of five years after filing or six months after presentation date; divisional with presentation date on/after Oct 30, 2019 — later of five years after filing or three months after presentation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the statutory time limits for filing an examination request for Category 3 applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination requisition due dates during transition (Oct 30, 2019)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner requisitions sent during the transition have different due dates: requisitions sent on/after Oct 30, 2019 — four month due date under subsection 131(1) of Patent Rules (SOR 2019-251); requisitions sent before Oct 30, 2019 — six month due date (or three months if special order) under former Patent Rules, even if due date falls after Oct 30, 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If abandonment occurs after Oct 30, 2019 from a requisition sent before Oct 30, 2019, deemed abandonment and reinstatement proceed under the former section 73 of the Patent Act as it read immediately before Oct 30, 2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of allowance and final fee — transitional due dates and reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of allowance under section 30 of the former Patent Rules sent before Oct 30, 2019 will have a six month due date even if that due date comes after Oct 30, 2019. Failure to pay the final fee on or after Oct 30, 2019 requisitioned in a notice of allowance dated before Oct 30, 2019 will result in deemed abandonment under paragraph 73(1)(f) of the Patent Act as it read immediately before Oct 30, 2019 and can be reinstated within 12 months under section 73(3) as it read before Oct 30, 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after allowance may be made under section 32 of the former Patent Rules where notice of allowance was sent before Oct 30, 2019, except where the application was abandoned for failure to pay final fee and subsequently reinstated. Otherwise, amendments after allowance are not permitted for Category 3 applications except to correct obvious errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of final fee upon reinstatement (Category 3 special rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 204 specifies that Category 3 applications abandoned under paragraph 73(1)(f) of the Patent Act as it read before Oct 30, 2019 and subsequently reinstated may have their final fee refunded upon a request received no more than 1 month after reinstatement, thereby returning the application to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The act of reinstatement alone returns the application to examination; no refund is required for that action. If final fee not refunded and upon re-allowance, the Commissioner will not require payment in a notice of allowance sent after reinstatement (subsection 204(b)). Refund does not automatically trigger return to examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees for patents and 12-month grace period (pre-Oct 30, 2019)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 78.55 specifies that section 46 of the Patent Act as it read immediately before Oct 30, 2019 applies to maintenance fee due dates (not including the period of grace) before Oct 30, 2019. If maintenance fee due date (not including period of grace) is before Oct 30, 2019 and fee not paid on or before due date, patentee has a 12-month grace period as per item 31 or 32 of Schedule II of the former Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional application of former grace period rules for maintenance fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national phase entry timing — 30-month rule and possible 12-month extension
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who designates Canada in an international application must meet subsection 154(1) requirements to enter the national phase not later than 30 months after the earliest priority date. If requirements not met by 30-month deadline, applicant may still enter within 12 months after that when additional requirements are met (reinstatement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See detailed PCT national phase entry requirements below (fees, copy, translation).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national phase entry requirements — fees, copy, translation
rubrics_metrics.description: To enter the PCT national phase within 30 months: Fees — pay basic national fee and all annual maintenance fees for anniversary dates before national phase entry; Copy if not published by WIPO — provide a copy of the patent application (RO/101 part of application); Translation — if description and claims entirely in a language other than English or French (other than sequence listing), submit a translation into English or French.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the PCT Applicant’s Guide and Canadian National Chapter for further details and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority date definition for national phase deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating deadlines to enter national phase in Canada, 'priority date' has the same meaning as Article 2(xi) of the PCT: the filing date of the earliest application whose priority is claimed, or the international filing date when there is no priority claim. The priority date may change only in three scenarios during the international phase (correction/addition under Rule 26bis.1; withdrawal under Rule 90bis.3; considered void under Rule 26bis.2(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if international filing date is more than 12 months after the earlier filing and priority is not restored, the priority date will still be used to calculate national phase entry time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of rights for national phase entry (requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application does not enter national phase in Canada within 30 months, the applicant has 12 months after that to reinstate rights under subsection 154(3). Requirements: request reinstatement of rights; provide a statement that the failure was unintentional; pay fees (basic national fee, fee for reinstatement, and all annual maintenance fees for anniversaries before national entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the international application is unpublished at national entry, provide a copy (RO/101 part). If description/claims entirely in a language other than English/French, submit translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension in case of attempted payment (within 12-month reinstatement period)
rubrics_metrics.description: If within the 12 months after the 30-month limit the Commissioner receives a communication clearly indicating the applicant’s intention to pay some or all of required fees, but not all required fees are paid within that period, those fees are considered paid on the day the communication was received provided the unpaid fees (including late fees) are paid within two months after the communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner is not obligated to inform the payer that part of the fees were missing, though the Office will endeavour to inform the applicant by a courtesy letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of untranslated elements at national phase entry
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may enter national phase with elements in a foreign language, but if translations of those elements (or part) are not provided on or before the national phase entry date, various consequences arise depending on which element lacks translation. Specifically, untranslated text will not be taken into account for interpreting the scope of protection being sought (see 12.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation of an Article 19 statement is not provided, the statement may be disregarded by the Commissioner. Providing a complete copy containing both translated text and text already in English/French can avoid needing translations of parts already in English/French.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requiring translation of complete copy (three-month compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant does not provide a translation of the abstract or Article 4 PCT request (RO/101), or does not provide a complete copy of description, claims, text in drawings, or language-dependent free text in sequence listing, the Commissioner may by notice require the complete translation no later than three months after the date of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with the notice will result in the application being deemed abandoned under subsection 132(1)(h) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of error in translations (conditions to replace a translation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant discovers an error in a translation submitted on or before national phase entry, the applicant may correct the translation before the day a notice of allowance or conditional notice of allowance is sent (or if withdrawn, before it's sent again) by submitting: the corrected translation, a request to replace the original, and statements that (a) at time of original submission it would have been obvious to a skilled translator that the original had an error and corrected translation is accurate, (b) error occurred despite due care, and (c) request is made within a reasonable time after awareness of the error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets objective factual showing required to replace a translation already filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: National phase entry date determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The national phase entry date is: the date on which the applicant complied with subsection 154(1) (and if applicable 154(2)) — if compliance occurred on different days, the latest of those dates; or the date on which applicant complied with subsection 154(3) — if different days, the latest of those dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When national phase entry date is established, Patent Office sends an acknowledgement of national phase entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open to public inspection (OPI) date for PCT national phase applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application is published in English or French by the International Bureau on or before its national phase entry date, the PCT national phase application is open to public inspection in Canada on the date of that publication. If published in another language, it is open to inspection when made publicly available in Canada.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPI date depends on publication language and availability in Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requiring establishment of applicant/representative (discrepancy in applicant names)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commissioner has reasonable grounds to believe the person who met national phase entry requirements is neither the applicant of the international application nor their legal representative, the Commissioner must send a notice under subsection 154(7) requiring that person to establish that they are the applicant or legal representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable evidence includes PCT/IB/306 showing a change of applicant, document effecting a transfer to that person, change-of-name document; Office may consider other submissions. A compliant request under subsection 154(6) to correct the naming error may also satisfy the notice. Failure to comply within three months means the person is deemed never to have complied with national phase entry requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of error in naming the applicant who paid basic national fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If Office records contain an error in naming the applicant who complied with national phase requirements, the error may be corrected on request of the person who paid the basic national fee. The request must state the error arose inadvertently, by accident or mistake, and without fraudulent/deceptive intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be made before the earlier of: (a) the later of three months after national phase entry date and, if a 154(7) notice was sent within that three months, three months after the notice; and (b) if Commissioner records a transfer under section 49, on or before day Commissioner received request to record transfer. A correction may create a discrepancy triggering a 154(7) notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability exceptions of Canadian patent legislation to PCT national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, PCT national phase applications are subject to Canada’s Patent Act and Patent Rules on the national phase entry date, but exceptions exist: subsections/sections not applying include subsection 27(7) (application fee not paid), section 27.01 (reference to previously filed application), section 28 (various filing requirements), section 28.01 (addition to specification/drawings), subsection 38.2(3) (language other than English/French), and subsections 78.1(2)/78.2 (definition/transitional filing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain administrative elements/requirements in Patent Rules are specific to PCT national phase applications (manner of appointment of patent agent, deemed appointment of common representative, requests for priority/restoration, corrections of applicant name). See relevant chapters for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time during international phase governed by PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 78 of the Patent Act does not apply to international applications during the international phase. Extensions of time are available only as provided under the PCT and Regulations under the PCT (including PCT Rules 80.5, 82 and 82quater).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed information about extensions of time during the international phase is in the PCT Applicant’s Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date of a PCT national phase application in Canada
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 161 states the filing date of a PCT national phase application is the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for priority/term calculations and other date-dependent provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of right of priority — receiving Office discretion and Canadian practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for restoration of the right of priority is a mechanism where time for filing may be extended beyond 12 months in limited situations (failure despite due care and/or unintentional failure). When CIPO acts as receiving Office, it will accept a request to restore priority if satisfied criteria are met; restoration may be effective in designated offices whose national laws provide for restoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PCT national phase applications with filing dates on/after Oct 30, 2019, restoration of priority that occurred prior to national phase entry will be deemed restored in Canada upon national phase entry. Applicants may also request restoration upon entry in Canada when filing date is on/after Oct 30, 2019. For regular Canadian patent applications and PCT national phases, request for restoration may be made when filing date of pending application is more than 12 months after the prior filing but within two months after the end of those twelve months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form to request national phase entry — RO/101 and no petition required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are not required to send a petition to the Patent Office for entry into the national phase in Canada. The National Chapter of the PCT Applicant’s Guide contains a Recommended Form (for request of Entry into National Phase under Article 22/39 — RO/101) that applicants may use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of RO/101 recommended for submitting national entry requirements and other information.

rubrics_metrics.name: All patent Office business is conducted in writing (Chapter 35 introduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: All business related to patent applications and patents before the Patent Office is done in writing: both submissions to the Office and correspondence from the Office. Chapter 35 is a guide to notices, letters and requisitions sent from the Office, encompassing most correspondence issued by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect written notices and requisitions; procedural compliance typically requires written responses within prescribed timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes from Patent Rules Amending the Patent Rules (SOR/2022-120)
rubrics_metrics.description: As of Oct 3, 2022: the excess claim fee applicable when requesting examination and when paying the final fee applies to applications for which examination was requested on/after Oct 3, 2022; a request for continued examination is required under subsection 85.1(1) for applications with examination requested on/after Oct 3, 2022; requests for continued examination made on/after Oct 3, 2022 require a subsequent request after two examiner reports; conditional notice of allowance under subsection 86(1.1) may be sent for applications on/after Oct 3, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These amendments change fee and continued-examination mechanics and allow conditional notices of allowance for applications affected.
